newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan state banks to offer T$200 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan state banks to offer T$200 bln loan.

text.p: The Taiwan Provincial Government has ordered seven state-run banks to jointly offer T$200 billion in loans by June 1997 to small and medium-sized businesses to boost economy, an official said on Thursday.

"Deputy Governor (of the provincial government) Lai In-jaw yesterday ordered presidents of the seven state banks to jointly offer T$200 billion in loan to help small and medium businesses in a slow economy," an official said by telephone.
"The Provincial Government will supervise the loan approval progress and demand effect by June 1997," he said.
The Land Bank of Taiwan will offer T$20 billion in loan, while each of the other six state banks will offer T$30 billion, he said.
The other six banks are Bank of Taiwan, Cooperative Bank of Taiwan, Medium Business Bank of Taiwan, Chang Hwa Bank, First Bank and Hua Nan Bank.
Taiwan has lowered its GDP growth forecast several times in the past few months due to a slowing economy.

The new cabinet, which took office in June, has taken various measures -- including cutting interest rates, conducting beneficial tax reforms and accelerating public construction projects -- to boost the slow economy, but such effort has not had a major effect so far.
The governmen statistics bureau in November forecast the island's GDP would grow 5.70 percent in 1996, lower than the actual 6.03 percent growth in 1995 and 6.54 percent in 1994.
However, the bureau predicted a recovering economy in 1997, seeing a GDP growth of 6.20 percent.
